documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
28M for his yearly check. Says he's fine, no visits anywhere else since last fall. Still never smoked; social drinking only.

ROS: negative, including no GI complaints, no palpitations, no headaches.

Exam: vitals reviewed, normal. Eyes, ears, throat normal. Heart with regular rhythm and normal S1/S2. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, no organ enlargement. Skin unremarkable. PHQ-2 = 0.

Impression: well adult.
- Flu vaccine administered today.
- Getting this year's COVID shot at his pharmacy next week.
- Dad's blood pressure history noted again; his own readings remain normal, recheck yearly.
RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record, 12/31/2024
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Visit date: 12/31/2024
Allergies: NKDA

CC: vomiting, cramping, watery stools since early this morning.

HPI: 28 y/o male, about 5 hours of nausea with repeated emesis, crampy abdominal pain and loose watery stool. Last night he was at a potluck on campus and ate several dishes; one was fried rice that he says sat out for several hours before it was warmed in a microwave. Others there who skipped the rice are well. Denies fever, hematochezia, travel.

PMH: none; no prior GI history. Meds: none.
FH: father HTN (dx 54); mother hypothyroid; no siblings.
SH: never smoker, 1-2 drinks/week, graduate student (public health).

VS: all within normal limits on arrival and recheck.
Exam: appears a little dry but alert and oriented x3. Abdomen soft, nondistended, mild diffuse tenderness, bowel sounds normal. No peritoneal signs.

Labs: CBC and BMP within normal limits.

MDM: short-incubation emetic illness after reheated rice, classic for Bacillus cereus toxin. No signs of invasive infection. Treated supportively with good response; tolerating PO before discharge.

Dx: Bacillus cereus food poisoning.
Dispo: home, oral fluids, bland diet, return for blood in stool, fever or inability to keep liquids down. Follow up with PCP as needed.

documents.title: ER on New Year's Eve
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted you to know I ended up in the ER the morning of the 31st with really bad vomiting and diarrhea. It started a few hours after a potluck — pretty sure it was some fried rice that had been sitting out. The ER doctor called it Bacillus cereus. They gave me supportive care and I went home that afternoon. I'm basically back to normal now, just a little wiped out. Do I need to do anything?

documents.title: RE: ER on New Year's Eve
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry to hear it — that's a rough way to end the year. That illness runs its course in a day or so, and you're past it. Keep drinking fluids and ease back into food. If you get fever, blood in the stool, or can't keep fluids down, call us or go back in. We'll ask the hospital for the ER note.

events.reason: motor vehicle collision, left upper quadrant pain

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST
Indication: restrained driver in MVC, LUQ pain, tachycardia, FAST negative.
Technique: axial images after intravenous contrast, portal venous phase, with multiplanar reformats.
Findings: Laceration of the spleen. No active contrast extravasation. No hemoperitoneum or free fluid. Liver, gallbladder, pancreas, adrenal glands and kidneys without injury. Bowel and mesentery unremarkable. No free air. Bladder unremarkable. Visualized lung bases clear. No acute fracture of the lower ribs, spine or pelvis.
reports.conclusion: Splenic laceration without active extravasation or hemoperitoneum. No other traumatic injury.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record, 07/12/2025
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT TRAUMA RECORD
Visit date: 07/12/2025
Allergies: NKDA

CC: LUQ pain and lightheadedness after car crash.

HPI: 29 y/o M, restrained driver, car left the road and hit a tree at moderate speed. Now with left upper abdominal pain and feeling dizzy. Seen here in December for a foodborne illness that resolved.

Meds: none. FH/SH: as previously recorded; never smoker, social alcohol, graduate student.

VS on arrival: BP 110/70, HR 105, RR 20, SpO2 97% RA.
Exam: alert. Abdomen soft, tender in the LUQ, without rebound or guarding. Normal bowel sounds. No flank bruising, no seatbelt sign. Chest wall nontender. Extremities without deformity.

Labs: Hgb 13.2, Hct 39.5, plt 250, WBC 9.0. Lactate 2.8.
FAST: negative for free fluid.

MDM: tachycardic with LUQ tenderness, mildly low Hgb and elevated lactate despite a negative FAST. CT A/P with contrast obtained: splenic laceration, no extravasation, no hemoperitoneum. Surgery consulted; nonoperative management with admission for serial hemoglobin.

Dx: traumatic splenic laceration, occult on FAST.
Dispo: admitted to the surgical service.

medications.sig: Take 1 to 2 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain. Avoid ibuprofen and naproxen.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Discharge Summary, 07/12-07/14/2025
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
SURGICAL SERVICE DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 07/12/2025, discharged 07/14/2025
Allergies: NKDA

Admission diagnosis: traumatic splenic laceration after MVC.

Hospital course: Admitted from the ED for nonoperative management. Bed rest overnight, serial hemoglobin checks remained stable, and his heart rate normalized by the next morning. No transfusion, no angiography, no operation. Advanced to a regular diet on hospital day 2, ambulating without dizziness. Pain controlled with acetaminophen.

Discharge medications: acetaminophen 500 mg, 1-2 tablets every 6 hours as needed. No NSAIDs.

Instructions: no contact sports, heavy lifting or strenuous exercise for 8 weeks. Return immediately for worsening abdominal pain, left shoulder pain, fainting or lightheadedness. Follow up with primary care within one week.

Condition at discharge: stable.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called: was in a car accident Saturday, hospitalized two nights for a torn spleen, sent home yesterday and told to see PCP within a week. Pain manageable with Tylenol, no dizziness, eating fine. Reviewed warning signs. Booked Thursday 7/17 at 10:20. Asked him to bring discharge papers.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
29M seen 5 days after an MVC. Per patient and the discharge paperwork he brought (hospital notes not yet received): restrained driver, car hit a tree; LUQ pain and lightheadedness in the ED; CT found a splenic laceration; observed two nights on the surgical floor with stable blood counts, no procedure. Sent home on as-needed acetaminophen with 8 weeks of activity limits.

Today: LUQ soreness improving, using acetaminophen once or twice a day. No dizziness on standing, no left shoulder pain, no lightheadedness. Eating and drinking normally.

Exam: vitals normal, not tachycardic. Mild LUQ tenderness without bruising, no guarding, no distension. Heart regular, lungs clear.

A/P
1. Splenic laceration, nonoperative, recovering as expected. CBC today. Continue acetaminophen as needed, no NSAIDs. No running, soccer or lifting until the 8-week mark. Reviewed reasons to go straight to the ED.
2. Records: will request the ED and inpatient notes.
3. Cleaned up the problem list — the December food poisoning has long resolved.

Recheck in early September.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Dylan, your blood count from yesterday is normal — hemoglobin 14.1, which is up from the hospital and right where it should be. That fits with the spleen healing on its own. Keep to the activity limits and I'll see you in September.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed request with signed release to the hospital's health information department for ED and inpatient records from 7/12-7/14/2025, plus the ED visit 12/31/2024.

documents.title: Hospital Records Received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hospital records arrived by fax: ED note 12/31/2024, ED trauma record and CT report 7/12/2025, discharge summary 7/14/2025. Filed to the corresponding dates and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Records Reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed. Hospital course matches what he told me. CT: splenic laceration without extravasation or hemoperitoneum; ED labs Hgb 13.2, lactate 2.8, since normalized Hgb here. December ED note consistent with Bacillus cereus. No action beyond the September visit.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Eight weeks out from the splenic laceration. No abdominal pain for about a month, stopped acetaminophen in late July. No lightheadedness. Itching to start running again.

Exam: well. Vitals normal. Abdomen soft, nontender throughout, no palpable spleen tip.

Assessment: splenic laceration healed clinically after nonoperative care.
Plan: OK to resume running now and build up over a couple of weeks; contact sports after that. Marked resolved. Physical next month with flu shot.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
29M, yearly visit. Back to running three days a week since September with no abdominal symptoms. Final year of the MPH. No meds. Never smoker, light social drinking.

Interval history: December ED visit for Bacillus cereus food poisoning; July MVC with splenic laceration managed without surgery, now healed.

ROS negative.
Exam: vitals normal. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, nontender, no splenomegaly. Skin clear. PHQ-2 0.

Plan:
- Flu shot today.
- COVID update at his pharmacy.
- Lipids were normal in 2021; no labs needed this year.
See him next October.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record, 02/27/2026
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Visit date: 02/27/2026
Allergies: NKDA

CC: profuse watery diarrhea after returning from Bangladesh.

HPI: 29 y/o M, known to this ED (foodborne illness 12/2024, splenic laceration after MVC 7/2025, both resolved). Got home 2/25 from two weeks of humanitarian work in Bangladesh, where he drank untreated well water and ate street food. Last evening developed sudden high-volume watery diarrhea, roughly hourly overnight, painless, no blood or mucus. Increasingly thirsty, lightheaded, cramping in the legs and hands. No fever, no abdominal pain, no recent antibiotics. Takes no medications.

FH: father HTN, mother hypothyroid. SH: never smoker, social alcohol, MPH student.

VS: BP 90/54, HR 116.
Exam: lethargic, eyes sunken, mucous membranes dry, cap refill delayed, hands and feet cool, skin turgor reduced. Abdomen soft, nontender, not distended. Stool observed: large volume, pale gray, watery, non-bloody, little odor — rice-water appearance.

Stool microscopy: no WBCs, no ova. Stool culture with Vibrio and toxin testing sent.

MDM: hypovolemic shock from severe secretory diarrhea after travel to an endemic area; cholera is the leading concern. Rapid IV fluid boluses started, admitted to medicine for ongoing volume replacement. Infection prevention and the state health department notified of a suspected case.

Dx: severe dehydration with hypovolemic shock; suspected cholera.
Dispo: admit.

conditions.label: Cholera due to Vibrio cholerae 01, biovar cholerae

medications.sig: Take 3 capsules (300 mg) by mouth once

results.text: Vibrio cholerae O1 isolated. Toxigenic strain.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Discharge Summary, 02/27-03/01/2026
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
HOSPITAL MEDICINE DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 02/27/2026, discharged 03/01/2026
Allergies: NKDA

Principal diagnosis: cholera (Vibrio cholerae O1, toxigenic) with severe dehydration and hypovolemic shock.
Prior history: Bacillus cereus food poisoning 12/2024; splenic laceration 7/2025, nonoperative.

Course: Arrived from the ED after initial IV boluses. Continued aggressive isotonic IV fluids with strict intake/output matching for the first day; blood pressure and heart rate normalized within hours. Transitioned to oral rehydration solution on day 2 as stool output fell. Given a single 300 mg oral dose of doxycycline once the clinical picture was clear. Diarrhea slowed markedly by the second night and stopped before discharge. Contact precautions maintained.

Microbiology: stool culture grew Vibrio cholerae O1, toxigenic (final 03/01). Case reported to the state health department.

Discharge medications: none.
Instructions: continue oral rehydration solution with any further loose stools, careful hand hygiene, no food preparation for others until stools normal. Follow up with PCP within a week.

documents.title: In the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Messaging from a hospital bed — got back from the Bangladesh trip on Wednesday and by Thursday night I had nonstop watery diarrhea. Blood pressure was low in the ER yesterday morning and they admitted me for IV fluids. They think it's cholera and are waiting on the stool culture. Feeling a lot better tonight. They said to see you after discharge.

documents.title: RE: In the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me, and glad tonight is better. Follow their fluid plan. Once you're home, message us and we'll get you in that week.

documents.title: Home + school note
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Home since Sunday. Culture on the hospital portal says Vibrio cholerae O1. Diarrhea stopped. Could you write a short note for my program covering classes I missed 2/26 through this week? Also want that follow-up visit.

documents.title: Medical Excuse Letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: To whom it may concern: Dylan Mazur was under medical care from February 26 through March 6, 2026, and was unable to attend classes or program activities during that time. He may return to normal activities on March 9. Please contact the office with any questions.

documents.title: RE: Home + school note
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Letter is attached under Letters. You're booked tomorrow, Wednesday, at 11:00.

events.reason: follow-up after hospital stay for cholera

conditions.label: Cholera due to Vibrio cholerae 01, biovar cholerae

documents.title: Post-Discharge Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
29M, three days after discharge. Hospital records not yet here; history from patient and his hospital portal.

Returned 2/25 from two weeks of humanitarian work in Bangladesh (untreated well water, street food). Abrupt torrential watery diarrhea from the evening of 2/26; ED 2/27 with low BP and fast pulse, admitted, IV fluids then oral rehydration, one dose of doxycycline. Stool culture final: Vibrio cholerae O1, toxigenic. Health department has already called him.

Now: last loose stool Saturday. Eating normally, drinking plenty, urine pale. No dizziness, cramps gone. No fever. No meds.

Exam: looks well, mucous membranes moist. Vitals normal, no orthostatic symptoms. Abdomen soft, nontender, normal bowel sounds.

A/P
1. Cholera with severe dehydration and hypovolemic shock, resolved. BMP today to confirm electrolytes and kidney function recovered. Hand hygiene; he knows the drill from public health school.
2. Request hospital records.
3. Letter for school sent yesterday.
Physical in the fall.
